designStatus: Original untested source-fit authoring programme; complete source/card/hard-path/all56-guide review with exact-hash receipts and interpretation limits. No actual learner observations or efficacy certification.

protocols.title: Notice and identify a real local place
protocols.task: Use a supervised accessible walk or equivalent dated local records, not a generic overseas worksheet. Identify living things, a land/water feature, a managed and built feature, a resource and actual social relationships. Compare two safe samples using a hand lens/access tool, naming observed similarities/differences. Add safe sky records identifying Sun, Moon, stars and a chart-confirmed planet; never look directly at the Sun. Retain all whole-card checks separately, including a microhabitat and map location. If checking the inherited land/water modelling prerequisite, actually construct an own model; interpreting a supplied map alone is not construction.
protocols.positiveEvidence: Specific observations support the identifications and distinguish what was actually seen from supplied representations. Natural/managed/built categories and role relationships are explained, not just named.
protocols.nearMiss: Naming only animals or only buildings; identifying every bright sky point as a star; describing a hand lens without actually using one.
protocols.transfer: Use another local patch and a new dated sky record; revise an uncertain identification using evidence.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit authoring design; no learner observations, intervention efficacy or whole-topic certification.

protocols.title: Relationships and attributed traditions
protocols.task: Use two non-sensitive supplied or voluntarily shared family/community cases, including a person caring for a living thing or shared place. Explain role, relationship and responsibility and how a changed circumstance affects it. Compare two attributed celebrations, include the meaning to participants and distinguish celebration from commemoration. No learner religious participation or family disclosure is compulsory.
protocols.positiveEvidence: A relation is explained using both sides, and a tradition is described as a practice meaningful to particular people. Changed roles and an environmental duty are retained.
protocols.nearMiss: A list of relatives/festival names; treating one community practice as every Indian family’s duty; assuming a feeling from tears or a smile.
protocols.transfer: Change the setting/person’s circumstance and use a contrasting local tradition; explain what remains and changes.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit authoring design; no learner observations, intervention efficacy or whole-topic certification.

protocols.title: Questions before the next observation
protocols.task: Prepare dated local seasonal records, local plant/leaf/flower comparisons, a supported simple food chain, community calendar practices and dated sky views. Have the learner choose at least three investigable questions, state a prediction BEFORE the next observation/record, choose observation/testing/research appropriately and compare with actual evidence. Include a monthly Moon sequence and three chart-confirmed planet positions about a week apart, using dated simulation when access/visibility prevents viewing. A ritual/calendar convention is not a natural law. Retain an actual safe indirect shadow-stick record where accessible, with dated backup records clearly identified. Complete the ordinary three-organism food-chain drawing with producer/consumer labels, correct food-to-feeder arrows and a supported knock-on prediction; plant-first describes this selected photosynthetic food-chain model, not every ecosystem on Earth. When checking inherited planet vocabulary, accept the accurate combined reference-frame explanation: the Moon goes around Earth while both also travel around the Sun.
protocols.positiveEvidence: Questions, prior predictions, method and later evidence are distinguishable. A mismatch is described honestly and a new prediction remains bounded by available information.
protocols.nearMiss: Adult supplies the exact question and answer; prediction is written after the result; assuming a universal four-season or festival calendar.
protocols.transfer: Use a contrasting locality or changed food-chain/plant case and explain which regularity can reasonably transfer.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit authoring design; no learner observations, intervention efficacy or whole-topic certification.

protocols.title: Trace a local service
protocols.task: Build an attributed local service board for family, school, bank, post office, market and a named Panchayat. Explain who does what, who uses it and why each matters; use a story, a labelled drawing and a table/report across the programme. For the Panchayat use an actually verified local/state case with elected representatives, Gram Sabha participation and funding including locally applicable rates/taxes/fees and other funds; never assume identical services or levies everywhere. RBI’s 2018 school booklet supports deposits/saving/interest conceptually, not current account eligibility, rates or a financial transaction. One available dated example is the MoPR-hosted Karnataka 2021 rules, notified in March 2022: service rates include water supply and a public notice/objection process. Use it as a dated state example of funding/participation, not current tax-rate advice or proof that every Panchayat has identical arrangements.
protocols.positiveEvidence: Each institution has a functioning role explanation and a relevant person–service relation. Bank savings/interest and more than one contribution to local services are explained through safe supplied cases.
protocols.nearMiss: Naming a building or copying a sign; treating post as buying goods only; asserting every Panchayat runs every listed council service; opening an account as a child task.
protocols.transfer: Follow a different service request and compare two localities’ arrangements while preserving the same institution/role operation.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit authoring design; no learner observations, intervention efficacy or whole-topic certification.

protocols.title: Make an object that actually works
protocols.task: Offer clean safe local card/fabric/reused materials and appropriate adult-supported tools. The learner chooses and independently makes an object for a declared display/classroom use, sketches or models a functional shape, tests it and explains a change. Across complete craft checks actually cut card AND fabric, fold/roll and make a joined standing/moving part, then tidy/store safely. A source-selected folded object is valid without implying every craft subskill was demonstrated in that one object.
protocols.positiveEvidence: Own making choices and functional check are visible; the object is usable/displayable for the stated purpose. Appropriate assistance/access is recorded without the adult making the whole object.
protocols.nearMiss: Ready-made item, adult-guided tracing only, a decorative drawing substituted for a functional object, or folding alone claimed as all cutting/joining evidence.
protocols.transfer: Make another useful object with different available material or revise the original to satisfy a changed use.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit authoring design; no learner observations, intervention efficacy or whole-topic certification.

protocols.title: Parts, connections and daily support
protocols.task: Create connected representations for water source/supply and river movement, Sun-driven water cycle, local seasonal conditions, plant/animal life cycles, a food/material product journey and transport, communication and household electricity. Explain a part-to-part connection and the life support/use in each. Retain actual build/test/improve of a safe low-power sound/light communication device and an appliance sort including mains/battery distinction; no child mains access. Whole life-cycle checks cover contrasting organism groups and stage diagrams, not one butterfly picture. Complete the water-cycle whole-card transfer with an actual safe covered-container observation, a named three-stage loop and the Sun’s role; distinguish a porous-ground puddle’s infiltration from evaporation. For appliances use at least ten declared examples and discuss hybrid/generator cases by actual power source; no opening household devices. Use side-by-side plant and animal generation models and the selected mammal/bird/amphibian/insect cases, including complete and incomplete metamorphosis. Reproduction starts a new generation; death does not cause birth, and not every individual reproduces. Diet examples use verified species evidence and do not assume the learner eats meat; a fox is not treated as an unqualified carnivore exemplar.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The learner traces a connected pathway/loop and explains what changes if a specified part/connection is unavailable, distinguishing a model from a measurement.
protocols.nearMiss: A disconnected object list; Sun “pulls water up”; visible cloud called invisible gas; communication treated as all sound being speech; unsafe mains demonstration.
protocols.transfer: Change a connection or locality and trace the implications using evidence rather than universal assumptions.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit authoring design; no learner observations, intervention efficacy or whole-topic certification.

protocols.title: Link a practice to its setting
protocols.task: Use attributed cases, including Madurai district’s account connecting Pongal with harvest, nature and cattle and a contrasting local work/food case. Identify the relevant environment/material/work and explain how it relates to a food or tradition; distinguish a participant’s meaning from a scientific causal claim. Check the actual local seasonal/crop account rather than generalise one district’s calendar or ritual to all India. Resource classification covers natural material, skills and equipment with scarcity choices.
protocols.positiveEvidence: A specific environment–livelihood–practice relationship is explained with its source and limits; another practice can differ without being judged inferior.
protocols.nearMiss: Merely name food/festival; claim all Indians celebrate the same way or that geography mechanically determines belief; import a climate calendar from another region.
protocols.transfer: Use a supplied contrasting locality and explain which relation changes and which evidence would establish it.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit authoring design; no learner observations, intervention efficacy or whole-topic certification.

protocols.title: Compare change using accounts and artefacts
protocols.task: Use a willing elder/community account or an attributed local story, plus dated objects/photos/maps/records. Compare a local occupation, food/resource use, celebration and communication across times, including a technology’s effect at home/work/travel. Explain a continuity and a change, what supports it and how two honest accounts can differ. Complete historical inquiry/vocabulary and text-inference checks remain separate; no Australian First Nations/migrant requirement is silently converted into Indian content.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The explanation connects changes to evidence and distinguishes account, inference and uncertainty; fewer surviving records can limit what is known.
protocols.nearMiss: Invented elder testimony; treating one story as complete history; listing “old/new” with no effect/reason; coerced family hardship/private disclosure.
protocols.transfer: Use a second account or surviving object that complicates the first explanation and revise the claim with a reason.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit authoring design; no learner observations, intervention efficacy or whole-topic certification.

protocols.title: Needs, support and protective action
protocols.task: Compare ordinary human and specified plant/bird/animal needs, including food/water/shelter, hygiene and suitable conditions. Use age-appropriate non-graphic supplied situations for unsafe behaviour or abuse: identify a trusted adult/help route, practise an optional protective response and explain that harm is never the child’s fault even if they freeze/cannot leave. Distinguish everyday traffic/water/online safety checks from nature care; do not stage danger or induce warning sensations.
protocols.positiveEvidence: A relevant need/protection and safe support action are explained for the actual case. Unsafe secrecy/reporting can be recognised without requiring a particular bodily alarm.
protocols.nearMiss: “All strangers bad, known people always safe”; blame for freezing; unsuitable animal feeding; a poster substituted for actual agreed hygiene practice.
protocols.transfer: Use another safe supplied case and identify who can help and how to keep telling until help arrives.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit authoring design; no learner observations, intervention efficacy or whole-topic certification.

protocols.title: Discuss and plan safely before an emergency
protocols.task: Use prepared adult-approved local panels for smoke/fire, minor injury/burn, electrical hazards, unusual heavy rain and a fallen tree. Obtain the plan from a family/community discussion OR an accurate supplied account; personal experience is never required. For each identify a warning, move/keep away from danger, an appropriate adult/local support route, adult responsibilities and safe preparations such as an accessible clear route/contact plan. Ask how a forecast supports preparation for at least two severe-weather cases. CBSE’s 2019 handbook supports adult-led preparedness, resource/route planning and inclusive support only; operational procedures/contacts must match the current local plan. No staged smoke, injury, flood or live electrical hazard, child first aid, fire extinguishing or rescue. Preparation reduces risk but does not guarantee safety; no blame follows when harm occurs. Retain the existing forecast topic’s inherited four-season whole-card check as a separate accurately attributed temperate-locality comparison, never a claim that every Indian locality has four such seasons.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The learner explains a relevant preparation with ordered steps/resources/support and why it helps, then discusses how another household/person’s access needs change the plan. Whole safety road/water/online and own planning checks remain separate.
protocols.nearMiss: Reciting “be careful”; an adult’s evacuation plan copied without explaining roles; saying “no” to fire as if every hazard were interpersonal; unauthorised technical treatment/repair.
protocols.transfer: Change a safe supplied situation, available route or support need; adapt preparation using the approved plan rather than invent a hazardous response.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit authoring design; no learner observations, intervention efficacy or whole-topic certification.

protocols.title: Make and enact a safety message
protocols.task: Choose appropriate school/local safety cases using accurate signs/actions. Actually produce readable short labels AND slogans with declared language/script, suitable display and audience. Explain why wording/image matches the action and enact a safe non-graphic roleplay using a provided scenario. Use newly acquired vocabulary in own speech and writing and change a message for a new audience; no fixed English word inventory or language mastery transfer is inferred.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The learner’s own displayed message communicates an appropriate action and their roleplay shows a matching safe/help response.
protocols.nearMiss: Only reading a ready-made sign, decorating without a safety meaning, producing a slogan with no enacted response or performing an unsafe emergency simulation.
protocols.transfer: Change the audience/location or hazard cue and revise both message and safe roleplay.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit authoring design; no learner observations, intervention efficacy or whole-topic certification.

protocols.title: Compare local living things
protocols.task: Make ethical local observations or use reliable dated records for plants, birds and other animals. Compare shape, sound where appropriate, food, growth/life stage and habitat. Record specific features, relate needs to conditions and explain a supported comparison; full organism groups/life-cycle diagrams remain separate whole-card checks. Unknown wildlife is observed at a distance; no required capture, forced touch or fabricated growth/sound.
protocols.positiveEvidence: Specific differences and similarities are tied to observed/attributed evidence across all required dimensions, acknowledging unavailable records.
protocols.nearMiss: A generic naming worksheet, adult-imposed guessed call, giving every plant the same requirements, or using one day’s size difference as a growth measurement.
protocols.transfer: Compare a new local pair or microhabitat and explain how an uncertain identification can be checked.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit authoring design; no learner observations, intervention efficacy or whole-topic certification.

protocols.title: Describe local differences accurately
protocols.task: Use attributed local accounts of foods, clothing and games and seasonal/harvest/sowing celebrations, including the Madurai harvest case as one example. Compare two practices and their participants’ meanings; establish local timing from records without assuming every crop, season or festival follows the same schedule. A provided family/community case can replace private disclosure; no worship, food tasting or animal sport is a performance demand.
protocols.positiveEvidence: Concrete similarities/differences are described accurately and respectfully, with a local seasonal/cultivation connection rather than a universal stereotype.
protocols.nearMiss: A national costume/menu stereotype, a festival name alone, universal January harvest for all India or pleasant feelings demanded as evidence.
protocols.transfer: Use an unfamiliar attributed local account and ask a respectful clarifying question before describing it.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit authoring design; no learner observations, intervention efficacy or whole-topic certification.

protocols.title: Follow resources into actual use
protocols.task: Trace actual nearby water, soil/plant/wood/mineral materials to daily uses and users. For a familiar product, sort natural material, human skill and equipment, trace making/transport/sale and explain a resource limit/choice with supplied simple cost data. These complete existing resource/supply-chain checks are separate from merely naming water as a resource. No actual purchase, paid work or child business is required.
protocols.positiveEvidence: A use and dependency are explained with a concrete material pathway and a relevant distinction among resource types.
protocols.nearMiss: Calling money a natural resource, treating all resources as fuels, or labelling a material with no use/pathway.
protocols.transfer: Change the available material or local supply and explain which choice/process must change.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit authoring design; no learner observations, intervention efficacy or whole-topic certification.

protocols.title: Share and care with real mechanisms
protocols.task: Carry out a safe practical shared-water/tree-care task, make an equitable access plan and explain maintenance/conservation. Combine sources on three actual contrasting efforts: Modhera’s 2022 solar-plus-storage project, the 2025 community-led groundwater/rainwater programme and ICAR’s Parasurampura millet/soil-moisture demonstrations. Explain an age-appropriate mechanism and individual/community relationship for each; compare limits instead of claiming universal success. Add a real local school/tree/water action, with adult-approved rainwater model/collection use (never presumed drinking water). Millets are a locally suitable crop option with conditional water/soil benefits, not zero-water, guaranteed-yield or medical advice. Retain the inherited resource claim’s actual obtain-and-combine-information operation, not only sorting renewable labels or recalling impacts.
protocols.positiveEvidence: Actual care/sharing is visible and the information account links action→mechanism→benefit for three real cases, with provenance and a stated limitation.
protocols.nearMiss: Conservation slogan alone, imaginary “real village”, sunlight stored as light in a panel, rainwater automatically potable or all millet crops needing no inputs.
protocols.transfer: Change a resource/access constraint and adapt the practical plan; explain why a project’s success does not imply it works identically everywhere.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit authoring design; no learner observations, intervention efficacy or whole-topic certification.

protocols.title: Support a specified living thing
protocols.task: Use a locally appropriate tree seed/young plant and reliable profile, plus separate bird and other animal cases. Identify actual soil/water/food/care needs, plan safe support, carry out and check a recurring appropriate action with supervision. Observe growth through dated records; compare seed/bulb starts separately. Do not feed wildlife arbitrarily, capture an animal or claim universal germination timing.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The support addresses the actual organism’s needs and is checked across appropriate occasions; a bean-only activity does not substitute for the selected tree duty inherited from earlier source tasks.
protocols.nearMiss: Naming a need without support, watering every species equally, handling an unknown animal or claiming observed growth from one snapshot.
protocols.transfer: Change the organism or condition and consult reliable care information before adapting support.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit authoring design; no learner observations, intervention efficacy or whole-topic certification.

protocols.title: Adjust resources and responsibilities fairly
protocols.task: Use supplied accessible scenarios involving differing mobility/access, resources, work distribution and shelter. Compare equal treatment with need-responsive fairness and propose a feasible adjustment, including how a role/duty changes with circumstances. Retain two-way perspective and vocabulary checks separately. No private diagnosis, hardship disclosure, charity performance or fixed gender/family division.
protocols.positiveEvidence: A specific need is identified, an adjustment fits it and the learner explains why it improves access/opportunity rather than only giving identical shares.
protocols.nearMiss: Diagnosing from appearance, “everyone same” regardless of access, assigning work by gender or assuming the affected person feels grateful/happy.
protocols.transfer: Use a new constraint and compare two reasonable adjustments with reasons.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit authoring design; no learner observations, intervention efficacy or whole-topic certification.

protocols.title: Reasons and action in shared places
protocols.task: Actually use an appropriate waste arrangement, take turns/queue, conserve shared water and care for a common space/property; discuss a safe supplied public-transport case and help across backgrounds when a genuine appropriate opportunity occurs. Explain reasons, participate in reviewing an agreement and distinguish consistent action from mere adult-watched compliance. Never manufacture another person’s distress or secretly surveil a child to “test” virtue. Concern/values remain contextual, not scored as positive mood.
protocols.positiveEvidence: Relevant action and reason are present with a changed-case explanation; context and limits of any actual observation are recorded.
protocols.nearMiss: Repeating a rule with no action/reason, a smile inferred as kindness, forced affection or an unsafe public task.
protocols.transfer: Change a shared-place/access situation and explain which norm/action should adapt and why.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit authoring design; no learner observations, intervention efficacy or whole-topic certification.

protocols.title: Interpret and make a usable local plan
protocols.task: Use actual simple plans of school and settlement/ward, including urban/rural alternatives as locally appropriate. Locate landmarks, explain a line plan and follow/describe routes. Draw own sketches with symbols/key/labels and consistent relative/cardinal directions; another person interprets a route and an ambiguity is repaired. A supplied reference plan is allowed; simply copying it is not own representation. Declare the viewer/landmark frame for positional language. Do not downgrade basic position competence for advanced dual relations or a viewpoint shift that the inherited guide explicitly defers; narrow diagnostic success is not the entire broader card.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The interpretation matches the actual key/directions and the learner’s sketch communicates locations/route clearly at the declared scale.
protocols.nearMiss: A memorised walk with no plan interpretation, a picture without spatial relationships/key or arbitrary left/right changes when rotating a page.
protocols.transfer: Change start point or rotate/change a plan key while making orientation explicit.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit authoring design; no learner observations, intervention efficacy or whole-topic certification.

protocols.title: Read maps across scales
protocols.task: Provide current approved simple city/state/country maps with dates, keys and orientation. Locate natural and built features and follow directions at each scale; use insets to connect own locality/region/state and label the state capital plus a regional centre for the existing whole claim. Trace an actual supplied food/service/transport interconnection across scales. Do not invent boundaries or replace Indian places with Australian mandatory facts.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The learner uses each map’s key/orientation and identifies scale/context before describing a feature or connection.
protocols.nearMiss: Copying a capital list, confusing a symbol with the actual size, transferring one map’s key blindly or memorising a route without reading.
protocols.transfer: Use a new map/key or a contrasting state and explain what changed and how to orient it.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit authoring design; no learner observations, intervention efficacy or whole-topic certification.

protocols.title: Actually investigate a question
protocols.task: Let the learner formulate/choose a specific question and choose observation, a one-change safe comparison/test or reliable research. Use appropriate simple equipment, describe/compare actual samples, make a prior prediction, gather data and answer using evidence. Do an independent OR a group option without treating either as universally required. Check practical risks, handle/clean equipment safely and explain a control. A surprising result is legitimate; no manufactured confusion/distress.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The method fits the question; actual data, observation and interpretation are distinguishable and support a bounded answer.
protocols.nearMiss: A memorised fact presented as an investigation, changing everything at once, adult-only equipment use or a post-hoc “prediction”.
protocols.transfer: Use a changed sample/question and justify a method/control/improvement.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit authoring design; no learner observations, intervention efficacy or whole-topic certification.

protocols.title: Show findings, not invented results
protocols.task: Use actual inquiry/local-source records. Organise a headed table, produce a graph/pictogram, a labelled observation diagram and both use and build a suitable simple classification key across the programme. Present the finding through at least two declared accessible modes including own oral AND written explanations with appropriate access/support across the programme; optional poem/play/skit remains a valid source alternative, not a compulsory art-form AND requirement. Distinguish what was seen from its explanation, give a supported conclusion, a new prediction and a method improvement. No automatic arbitrary-language mastery. Records may come from systematic observation rather than a controlled experiment; no one-variable-test requirement is inferred for all recording simply from an inherited hard path.
protocols.positiveEvidence: Representations reflect actual records and the conclusion answers the question with evidence/provenance; the learner can explain a changed-case prediction and limitation.
protocols.nearMiss: Neat invented data, graph with no source, memorised poem unrelated to findings or an interpretation called a direct observation.
protocols.transfer: Present the same evidence to a new audience/format and check whether the meaning and uncertainty survive.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit authoring design; no learner observations, intervention efficacy or whole-topic certification.

protocols.title: Connect matter, energy and systems concretely
protocols.task: Use safe room-temperature materials and adult-controlled mild warming/cooling records, not child boiling experiments. Compare solids/liquids/gases by observable behaviour, including particulate-solid sand and invisible water vapour versus visible droplets. Complete inherited particle models as representations, not direct sight of particles. Observe actual energy-transfer evidence for sound, light, gentle heat and a safe low-voltage battery circuit; sound at a comfortable level can be evidenced by hearing at a destination; if a separate-object vibration demonstration is chosen, control direct mechanical contact and other causes rather than assert airborne transfer from touching alone. Trace source→destination, connected system parts and method/evidence across cases. Retain the existing whole energy assessment’s distinction: current/charge circulates in the loop while energy is delivered/transferred; a supplied protected adult-set meter comparison is one permitted check, not a new universal NCERT measurement duty. Battery equipment is adult-selected and protected low voltage: no loose button cells, exposed lithium cells or opening appliances. Matter classification actually covers at least eight examples with behavioural reasons; inherited particle diagrams are marked as models, with safe mild-temperature records for changes of state. In a melting plateau at constant temperature, do not require particles to speed up: added energy can change the state. Keep observable classification distinct from a microscopic model and never infer the full particle/state inventory from one narrow diagnostic.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The learner uses observations/models appropriately and explains a shared idea in a new concrete case without importing advanced laws.
protocols.nearMiss: A state label based only on appearance; visible white “steam” treated as gas; sound demonstration with direct touching mistaken for airborne transfer; a circuit diagram without actual complete circuit.
protocols.transfer: Change a material/system/transfer pathway and explain what evidence would distinguish alternatives.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit authoring design; no learner observations, intervention efficacy or whole-topic certification.

protocols.title: A representative science and design portfolio
protocols.task: Compose local living-needs/life-cycle evidence, safe push/pull observations, sky/Earth-space representations and a functional engineering task. Design/build/test a safe ramp or other push/pull solution for a stated target, record data, modify and retest; explain how shape/structure supports function. Relate a natural-science idea to a practical application. Offer accessible response modes and sufficient time across the stage; this is representative foundational familiarity, not an exam covering every later course.
protocols.positiveEvidence: Actual evidence and a working tested/refined model support an age-appropriate explanation and cross-case connection.
protocols.nearMiss: Naming science branches, looking at a finished model only, equating a failed first design with no learning, or demanding advanced mechanics to pass a concrete primary task.
protocols.transfer: Use a new design constraint or compare another practical application and identify what evidence/test is useful.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit authoring design; no learner observations, intervention efficacy or whole-topic certification.

protocols.title: Goal local world
protocols.task: Complete every named child protocol with its actual performance, source and access conditions. Then use a new connected local case to explain how the evidence/components work together; do not certify the broad goal by counting tags or checking only the easiest child.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The composed portfolio covers every relevant child duty and supports an independent transfer explanation; broad orientations remain contextual where declared.
protocols.nearMiss: A short goal summary substituted for child tasks, one component taken as the whole goal or pleasant affect mistaken for demonstrated understanding.
protocols.transfer: Use a new appropriate local situation and trace a justified connection across completed components.
protocols.evidenceStatus: Original untested source-fit authoring design, not learner attainment.
